newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - June 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - June 4.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian Football League and Sydney Swans star Tony Lockett will undergo groin surgery tomorrow and will be out for a possible six weeks. Lockett has only played one full game this year, however, but it is believed he is staying positive about his situation. Page 20.

Shane Warne has been included in the Australian Test team to face England in the first Ashes Test. It is hoped Warne can repeat his Monday performance, when he bagged seven wickets against Derbyshire without even using his most dangerous weapon, the fiercely spun leg break. Page 19.

The Australian Women's Hockey team, the Hockeyroos, are level leaders with the United States at the Champions Trophy, being held in Berlin, Germany. The lead comes after the Australians beat the Netherlands 2-0, with Alyson Annan scoring her second goal in two matches. Page 16.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Tennis player Patrick Rafter is on his way to the quarter finals of the French Open after defeating fellow Australian Mark Woodforde. The match was an emotional one for both Woodforde and Rafter who are Davis Cup team mates, as well as for Davis Cup coach Tony Roche. Page 46.

Queensland State of Origin coach Paul Vautin has provided his team with some motivation to win next Wednesday's match, saying he will quit if they lose. Vautin, speaking at a press conference yesterday, said two series losses would amount to him not being reinstated as coach next year, and him not seeking the position. Page 45.

Australian javelin thrower and Olympic silver medallist, Louise McPaul, has come out of a four month injury break to qualify for the world championships being held in Athens in August. McPaul has a crippling back injury and did not even get through the warm-up at the trials without her back grabbing, but she still threw 61.56 metres to qualify for the team. Page 44.
THE AGE

Monday night AFL in Melbourne is to be reduced to three matches next year, with the league expected to move more matches interstate to the warmer climates of Sydney, Brisbane and Perth. This is in keeping with the recent decision to move the Monday June 1 match to the day before, partially to give the players a break before the State of Origin series, and partially because of expected low crowd numbers. Page B16.

Craig Ellis was selected for the State-of-Origin match yesterday. Before this Ellis was going to give up the game because of constant injury, and bad form last year. Ellis is one of ten Western Bulldogs selected in the State of Origin squads, the others include Jose Romero, Tony Liberatore and Simon Minton-Connell. Page B16.

The proposal to put all of Australia's 1600 golf clubs on-line by next year with a computerised handicapping system, is in danger of being scrapped. Golf Access, a partner with the Australian Golf Union in the project, has gone into voluntary administration, putting the project on hold. Page B14.
THE HERALD SUN

Victorian State-of-Origin coach Lee Matthews has warned South Australian fans that the future of State-of-Origin football depends on them. Matthews believes if there is a lock-out crowd at Football Park on June 21, the AFL could dismiss the club lobby who boycotted the WA-SA clash at Football Park last year, saying State-of-Origin was not relevant. Page 70.

Melbourne Demons five time premiership player, coach, board member and president, Ian Ridley, announced his retirement from the club board last night. Ridley has emphasised the move is a retirement and not a resignation, but did speak out against the sacking of demons coach Neil Balme last week. Page 69.

Champion horse trainer Lee Freedman has declared his Queensland Derby contenders to be a cut above the top three-year-olds. Freedman has backed Marble Halls as better than retired Victorian Derby winner Portland Player, and Graeme Rogerson's AJC Australia Derby winner Ebony Grove. Page 66.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Olympic swimming silver medallist Scott Miller has been expelled from the Australian Institute of Sport after an altercation at a Canberra nightspot involving Miller and fellow swimmer Toby Haenen. The pair are now both in doubt for the Pan Pacific team after alcohol was found in their systems, a substance banned at the AIS. Page 76.

Following rumours that he may be sacked at the end of the year because of constant injury and little playing, Canberra Raiders management have assured half-back Ricky Stuart the rumours have no substance. It is believed they will also have to assure Bradley Clyde of his position, after the same rumours surfaced about him. Page 72.

Australian batsman Matthew Hayden has scored his third century in three days for Hampshire against Warwickshire. Hayden's form has shown the Australian Ashes side just what they are missing, with him scoring a six and 17 fours in his innings of 119. Page 80.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
